The proposed solution is incorrect. 

Specifically, the claim that $v(4, \sqrt{2}) = 13$ is false because there exists a connected 4-regular graph on $14$ vertices with second largest eigenvalue $\lambda_2 = \sqrt{2} \le \sqrt{2}$.

Such a graph is given by the incidence graph of the complement of the Fano plane (the unique symmetric $(7, 4, 2)$-design):
- It has $7 + 7 = 14$ vertices and is connected and 4-regular.
- Its incidence matrix $B$ satisfies $BB^T = (k - \lambda)I + \lambda J = 2I + 2J$.
- The eigenvalues of $BB^T$ are $16$ (multiplicity 1) and $2$ (multiplicity 6).
- Consequently, the eigenvalues of its bipartite adjacency matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & B \\ B^T & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ are $\pm 4$ (multiplicity 1 each) and $\pm \sqrt{2}$ (multiplicity 6 each).

Thus, $\lambda_2 = \sqrt{2} \le \sqrt{2}$, which proves $v(4, \sqrt{2}) \ge 14 > 13$.

VERDICT: REJECT
